course: Stanton County Prairie Pines Golf Course — 50 N. Airport Rd, Johnson (Johnson City), KS 67855
notes:
HOLES: 9 holes, par 35. Confirmed by GolfPass, GolfLink, 9holegolfcourses, SupremeGolf and the course listing itself. Opened 1977 (GolfPass, Golfify; one GolfLink-derived summary said 1979).

SECOND SET OF TEES FOR 18: No. There is no separate second-nine tee set. An 18-hole round is the same nine played twice from the same tees. Evidence: 18Birdies lists the 18-hole course as 6,414 yds / rating 69.8 / slope 122 — exactly 2x the Blue nine (3,207 yds, 34.9) with the Blue slope carried over; mScorecard lists "total par 70" (2x35) against a single 9-hole card. No source anywhere lists a distinct set of back-nine yardages. The course's own green-fee page is a flat daily rate ($15 weekday / $20 weekend/holiday), not split 9 vs 18, which is consistent with a single loop played once or twice.

COURSE'S OWN SITE PUBLISHES NO SCORECARD. stantoncountyks.com/prairie-pines-golf-course and its "Membership & Green Fees" subpage carry only contact info, board/staff, membership rates ($275 in-county single / $375 family / $475 out-of-county) and green fees — no per-hole data, no scorecard PDF. So there is no course-authoritative per-hole number to defer to; everything below is database-sourced and cross-checked.

PER-HOLE YARDAGE: taken from mScorecard, the only source with all three tees hole-by-hole. Its column totals (3,207 / 2,996 / 2,784) reconcile exactly with 18Birdies, GolfPass, GolfLink and 9holegolfcourses, and its per-hole White row (352/187/458/348/352/330/308/141/520 = 2,996) matches GolfLink, 9holegolfcourses, 18Birdies and Golfify hole for hole. High confidence on par and on White/Blue/Red yardages.

TEE NAMES: reported as Blue / White / Red, the colors published by 18Birdies and GolfPass. mScorecard prints the same three columns as "Championship / Regular / Ladies" (Championship = Blue 3,207, Regular = White 2,996, Ladies = Red 2,784). Since no photo of the physical card could be found, either naming may be what is actually printed on it.

STROKE INDEX — NOT REPORTED (handicap set to 0). Three databases publish three mutually incompatible sets, so any one of them would be a guess:
  - 18Birdies (printed as an 18-hole odd index, 1-17): 7, 3, 1, 11, 5, 17, 15, 13, 9 — equivalent to a 9-hole order of 4, 2, 1, 6, 3, 9, 8, 7, 5.
  - Golfify: 7, 2, 1, 9, 4, 6, 5, 8, 3.
  - Hole19: 4, 9, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 7, 6.
  Only hole 3 (the 458-yd par 4) is agreed on as stroke index 1. The Hole19 set looks machine-generated (indexes 1-2-3 land on consecutive holes 3-4-5, and it makes the 187-yd par 3 the easiest hole). If a stroke index is needed, call the pro shop at (620) 492-6818 — that is the only way to get the printed card.

OTHER SOURCE DISAGREEMENTS:
  - White course rating: 34.1 (18Birdies, a true 9-hole rating) vs 35.0 (GolfPass and GolfLink). 34.1/115 is used above because 18Birdies is the only source publishing per-tee, per-gender ratings and its Blue figure (34.9) doubles cleanly to the 69.8 18-hole rating. The 35.0 figure looks like a rounded or mis-keyed value repeated between sites.
  - Red total: 2,784 (18Birdies and mScorecard, and mScorecard's holes sum to it) vs 2,804 (GolfPass). Hole19 shows a different "Ladies" card entirely — 2,740 total, holes 322/171/419/318/322/302/282/129/475 — roughly 20-40 yds short on every hole. Treat Hole19's red numbers as a separate (likely re-measured or mis-entered) dataset; 2,784 is the consensus.
  - Red women's rating/slope is 35.8/123 (18Birdies); the 33.3/108 in the structured output is the men's Red rating, matching the men's figures given for Blue and White.

RENOVATION / RE-ROUTING: none reported by any source. A 2018 Kansas Golf Book write-up describes the same open layout ("wide open fairways, prairie grass, scattered trees") and every yardage set published since matches the numbers above, so a mismatch against an aerial map is unlikely to be explained by a rebuild. Note the address is sometimes listed as "E Hwy 160 & Airport Rd" (18Birdies) rather than 50 N. Airport Rd — same site.

BLUEGOLF: could not be used. course.bluegolf.com serves its detailed scorecard behind an AWS bot-verification/CAPTCHA wall, so it was not available as a cross-check.
